credits.name: AirLLM

credits.name: OpenBot

credits.name: Liquid d1.2
credits.role: decision model behind web_task: Fennec's own browser loop asks it for one operation + element index per step. Paid hosted API, needs LIQUID_API_KEY, called over HTTPS by fennec-core/liquid.py; nothing is cloned or installed for it

credits.name: browser-harness
credits.role: the CDP transport the Fennec loop drives Chrome with, installed from PyPI (pinned 0.1.13, the version whose browser_harness.helpers.cdp and browser_harness.admin.ensure_daemon the loop imports) into Fennec's own venv at ~/.fennec/browser-tools/fennec/.venv; it is a dependency of the lane, never of core, so the interpreter the apps run on stays clean

repos.description: Fennec, the native Rust engine and the suite's only engine: cargo build --release produces target/release/fennec(.exe), launched directly with the serve/run/info/plan/doctor verbs. `fennec update` and the hub's --update fast-forward this checkout with git pull --ff-only like every other repo.

Shared Python orchestration runtime (engine supervision, ACP, outlets, compatibility routes); pyproject supplies fastapi, uvicorn, psutil and the fennec-agent console script. It is not the coding-agent PWA front door.
Native Rust CLI (cargo build --release): the `fennec` launcher in one crate. Nothing is pip-installed here - only the core is a Python package.

Native Rust/GPUI desktop application: the suite's one desktop window, `fennec-desktop-gui`, built with cargo build --release --features gui. The earlier egui binary is historical A/B material, not a fallback.
Canonical Rust/Axum coding-agent backend and the PWA it serves on 127.0.0.1:8787 (falling back to :8788 when occupied); also the native Nod stdio endpoint and the opt-in Obsidian local-vault writer.
Shared gpui-kit UI crate (theme presets, markdown rendering, message/queue widgets, workspace dialog) path-depended on by fennec-desktop.

The one Rust implementation of context compaction (elide / dedupe / budget) plus the token-saving mods, path-depended on by fennec-cli, fennec-desktop and fennec-coding-agent, so every cargo build in the suite needs this checkout beside its own.
IDE integration; plugin packaging is a separate step.
Upstream OpenBot coworker workspace, cloned only. The user installs its dependencies and runs it; Fennec talks to its existing loopback AG-UI routes and never edits, patches, vendors or starts it.

inference.description: Local Fennec engine (native Rust, cargo build --release) and command-line runtime; Fennec is the only engine, so an unbuilt checkout is reported as missing, never replaced by another engine.

desktop.description: Native Rust/GPUI desktop on the Rust coding-agent backend and engine; pip deps are the local STT sidecar.

coding-agent.description: Local inference plus the Rust/Axum coding-agent server and web UI; pip deps are the local STT sidecar.

jetbrains.description: Local engine and agent for the IDE plugin; pip deps are the local STT sidecar.

speech.description: Local speech-to-text sidecar (faster-whisper CPU) for the core and PWA; av<18 because PyAV 18 removed metadata_errors.

npu.description: Accelerator sidecar packages (device probe + batched code index) for the interpreter the apps use; the embedding model is a prebuilt OpenVINO IR download, so optimum-intel and torch are never installed here. Never native token decoding.

fine-tune.description: Explicit opt-in to large training dependencies.

mobile.description: Rust coding-agent backend + PWA on the same device (Termux phone or desktop); the local engine starts on demand; pip deps are the local STT sidecar.

browser-outlets.description: web_task and coworker_task. web_task is Fennec's own loop on a Liquid d1 model: the hosted d1.2 is a paid API needing LIQUID_API_KEY, the free open-weight d1-2B needs a local LIQUID_ENDPOINT; plus the browser-harness transport, which this feature installs into a venv of its own under ~/.fennec/browser-tools/fennec/.venv instead of into the interpreter the apps run on. coworker_task is OpenBot, cloned only - never modified, patched, vendored, given dependencies or started by this hub.
